title: The Spy in the Shanghai Office
synopsis: Shanghai, 1920: Korea's government in exile works in a small office.
At night, someone sits at the desk with the secret list.
Kim Gu, the police chief, needs proof.
goal: Find out who copied the secret list, and show the police chief the proof.

notes: A time worked out from Haesu's note: the light went on at eleven; half of a four-hour candle burned, two hours; the light went out at one in the night, 01:00.
Haesu, the candle and the light are made up.

clueInputs.note: The keepers' letter box came to Shanghai with Haesu.

learning.objective: at eleven, burns for four hours, half of it was gone을 읽고 불이 꺼진 시각(01:00)을 계산한다.
expressions: A new candle burns for four hours.
This morning, half of it was gone.

play.title: Half a Candle
story: Early morning in a narrow Shanghai lane.
A young clerk hurries past you and drops a folded note.
It is in Hangeul, with a small water drop in the corner.
play.letter:
Detective, someone used the list desk last night.
The guard saw a light in the office window at eleven.
I left a new candle there. A new candle burns for four hours.
This morning, half of it was gone.
— a small water drop
play.question: What time did the light go out? Count the hours, then put in the time as a number.
hints: Find when the light went on, and how much of the candle burned.
Half of four hours is two hours. Count on from eleven at night.
play.successMessage: The light went out at one in the night!
transition: Someone sat at the list desk from eleven until one.
The young clerk comes back. "I am Haesu. I wrote that note."
"Gyeongsun of Aunae is my cousin. She gave me the old box."

feedback.1300: It was night, not the afternoon. One in the night is 01:00.
feedback.2300: Eleven is when the light went ON. When did it go out?
feedback.0300: Only half of the candle burned, not all of it.

play.orderFeedback: The right numbers, in the wrong order. Hours first, then minutes.

play.title: The Police Report
story: Kim Gu's police searched it at dawn.
play.letter:
The key is next to the stove. It opens the list desk.
The ink bottle is on the window sill. It is normal office ink.
The thin paper is under the list desk. Names are pressed into it.
— Kim Gu's police

hints: Read each line of the report. Each one says where a thing is.
Copying presses names through the paper. Which thing has names pressed into it?
transition: Someone laid thin paper on the list and wrote over it.
The names are pressed into the paper, but not inked.
Haesu frowns. "Only clerks can come in at night."

play.title: The Sign-Out Book
story: By the door hangs the clerks' sign-out book.
Every clerk writes the time they go home.
play.letter:
Haesu: left at nine.
Mr. Pak: left at ten.
Mr. Seo: left at half past eleven.
Mr. Nam Giho: left at a quarter past one.
The night guard: here all night, at the front door.
play.question: Who was still in the office when the light went out? Type his name.

transition: Mr. Nam Giho came to the office only last month.
His desk is empty this morning.
Haesu runs to find the police chief.

notes: Kim Gu's four questions, each answered by one mission's evidence: when (Haesu's note), how (the police report), who (the sign-out book), and what his police are for (the police report again: guarding the government and watching for spies, h3). The talk ends on that history: the answer 'protect'.
Kim Gu is real; every word he says is made up (dossier fiction), resting on h1-h3. The spy, the list and the clerks are made up.

play.title: The Police Chief
story: A big man in a dark suit comes up the stairs.
"I am Kim Gu," he says. "I am the police chief here."
"Haesu told me what she saw. Show me your proof."
play.letter:
The light burned at the list desk from eleven until one.
Thin paper under the desk: names pressed into it.
Mr. Nam Giho left at a quarter past one.
The police guard the government and watch for spies.
play.question: Answer the police chief's questions with your evidence.
hints: Show one piece of evidence for each question.
Use Haesu's note, the police report and the sign-out book. One of them is used twice.
transition: Kim Gu locks the real list in an iron box.
"Haesu," he says, "you saw the first clue. Thank you."
Haesu puts her note in the old wooden box. One more water drop.
play.orderFeedback: Show one piece of evidence for each question.

evidence.name: Kim Gu's Case Note
evidence.description: The police chief's note: the list was copied. Haesu saw the first clue.

intro: Autumn, 1920. You are a guest of Kim Gu in Shanghai.
After the March First Movement, Koreans began a government here in April 1919.
It is the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea.
Kim Gu is its police chief. He keeps it safe from spies.
This morning, he is worried. "Someone was at our secret list," he says.
play.caseSummary: A light burned at the list desk from eleven until one. Thin paper showed the list was copied. Mr. Nam Giho, a new clerk, left last. Haesu, a keeper, saw the first clue. The Provisional Government began in Shanghai in April 1919, and Kim Gu was its police chief. His police guarded it and watched for spies. Later, in 1940, Kim Gu became its head.

notes: PART 10 Case 09 (Act 3 opens): Haesu, a young clerk and keeper, brings the keepers' box (s5_ep08_e4) to Shanghai; her portrait and Kim Gu's are planned here once and reused in Case 10.

Kim Gu is real; his words are made up (dossier fiction). The spy Nam Giho, the list, the clerks, the candle and the police report are made up. The case ends on history: the Provisional Government founded in Shanghai in April 1919 and Kim Gu's police (h1-h3).
